content:
marta: heads up — prod GPU pool A p99 spiked around 09:13 UTC. p99 ~1.8s (was ~0.28s), throughput down ~30% on the long‑seq slice. Noticed a lot of kernel handoffs in the runtime logs and a KV-cache eviction burst. anyone looking?
kevin: pulling flameprof and kernel-selection traces now. early glance shows fallback_attention getting chosen for many requests with seq>1024 — kernel chooser switched after a shape hint.
kevin: snippet from profiler: ```kernel=optimized_attention calls=22 avg=0.22ms
kernel=fallback_attention calls=410 avg=1.15ms
queue_depth spike at 09:12:46```
raj: @marta can we route long‑seq traffic to the quantized path (q8/q4) temporarily? that'll reduce kernel mismatch and lower p99 while we debug. Also consider lowering max batch size for that pool.
sophia: KV cache logs show evictions from tenant=search-surge-7 during the same window — short bursts of many different prefixes. looks like cache churn causing more misses and longer compute paths.
anas: suggested immediate mitigations: 1) enable feature flag runtime.kernel_strict_pin to prefer optimized kernels when available, 2) apply a soft throttle for tenant=search-surge-7 (50rps) to limit KV churn, 3) route seq>1024 to dedicated lane using model_variant=ggml-13b-q4. want to roll those in sequence.
incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-042 — "prod pool A p99 spike + throughput drop" — severity: P2. Assignee: eng-runtime oncall.
marta: doing 1) toggle kernel_strict_pin now (ff:runtime.kernel_strict_pin=true). will watch for regressions.
deploy-bot: feature flag runtime.kernel_strict_pin set to true in prod by marta at 09:18:12 UTC.
kevin: after the flag flip, kernel selection stabilized for ~80% of long seqs — fallback calls dropped ~70%. p95 improved quickly, p99 moving down but still a bit noisy.
sophia: applying tenant throttle (rate-limit) to search-surge-7 now: policy: rate=50rps, burst=200.
anas: also bumped kvcache.pin_ttl from 30s -> 120s for pool A to reduce eviction churn. doing that via runtime config sync.
kevin: watching profiler again — optimized_attention calls increased, avg latency for longseq down to ~0.45ms per token on hot path. overall request latency p99 trending to ~0.42s.
marta: routing seq>1024 to ggml-13b-q4 variant (dedicated lane) starting canary 10% then 100% if OK.
sophia: canary looks good for 10% — no errors, throughput stable. bumping to 100%.
incident-bot: INC-2026-042 status update: mitigations applied (kernel pin, tenant throttle, kvcache ttl bump, longseq routing). Monitoring p95/p99.
raj: postmortem action items: - improve kernel chooser heuristics to consider recent runtime histogram, - add kvcache churn alerting (eviction rate per tenant), - add automated temporary routing to quantized lane on kernel-mismatch spikes.
marta: agree. small follow-ups: create a playbook entry for "kernel handoff + kv churn" and add runbook commands to toggle the kernel_strict_pin ff and tenant throttles.
kevin: saved profiler traces at s3://redwood-profiles/prod/INC-2026-042/{trace1,trace2}.zip for root cause analysis.
anas: monitoring shows p99 back to 0.38s and throughput recovered ~95% baseline. closing active mitigation in 10m, will keep throttles in place until tomorrow morning unless noise returns.
incident-bot: INC-2026-042 resolved (mitigated) at 09:25:60 UTC by marta. follow-up: postmortem scheduled in #postmortems.
marta: thanks team — will draft a short postmortem + improvement tickets tomorrow. :thumbsup:
